text: `List` displays a navigable sequence of items.
evidence: Build creates one row per visible item and List.Keybinds provides navigation.

text: A list containing Inbox, Today, and Upcoming.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `NewListState` stores the items, cursor position, and selection.
evidence: Constructor initializes Items, CursorIndex, and Selection signals.

text: `SetItems`, `Append`, `InsertAt`, and `RemoveAt` update the items.
evidence: These methods mutate the Items signal and maintain cursor bounds.

text: `SelectedItem` returns the item at the cursor, while `SelectedItems` returns the multi-selection.
evidence: SelectedItem indexes CursorIndex; SelectedItems iterates Selection keys.

text: Up and Down, or `k` and `j`, move the cursor.
evidence: The four keys bind keyCursorUp and keyCursorDown.

text: Home and End jump to the first and last visible items.
evidence: Home binds keyCursorToFirst; End uses the last filtered view index.

text: Enter and a double-click call `OnSelect`, or `ActivateOnClick` enables single-click activation.
evidence: Keybinds binds enter to selectItem; handleMouseDown invokes OnSelect for ActivateOnClick or repeated clicks.

text: With `MultiSelect`, Shift navigation, Shift-click, and dragging extend the selection.
evidence: Conditional shift keybinds call range selection; mouse handlers select ranges when MultiSelect is true.

text: The default renderer formats each item with `fmt.Sprintf("%v", item)`.
evidence: Build formats the item before constructing presented text.

text: `RenderItem` receives the item and its active and selected flags.
evidence: The field type is func(item T, active bool, selected bool) Widget.

text: `Filter` and `MatchItem` control filtering, while `RenderItemWithMatch` also receives the match result.
evidence: List.Build computes or reuses the filtered view and passes each cached match to RenderItemWithMatch, which takes precedence over RenderItem.

text: `List` computes the filtered view during rendering. `State.ApplyFilter` can compute it earlier, and `FilteredCount` reports the last computed view size.
evidence: Build computes or reuses cached view indices; ApplyFilter can populate the cache ahead of Build; FilteredCount reads the stored view length.

text: `CursorIndex` and selection indices refer to the source items even when filtering changes the visible order.
evidence: Navigation maps visible indices to source indices; SelectedItems indexes the original Items signal using selection keys.

text: `OnSelect` receives one item. Multi-selection is available separately through `State.SelectedItems()`.
evidence: The callback takes T only; SelectedItems separately walks Selection in source order.

text: A shared `ScrollState` connects the list to a surrounding `Scrollable` and keeps cursor movements in view.
evidence: revealCursor derives the cursor region and updates the supplied ScrollState.

text: [Table](table.md) displays rows in columns.
evidence: Table has Columns and constructs cells for each row.

text: `Table` displays navigable rows and columns.
evidence: Build constructs a tableContainer with per-row, per-column cells.

text: A table with Name and Role columns and three people.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `NewTableState` holds the rows, cursor, and selection.
evidence: Initializes Rows, CursorIndex, CursorColumn, and Selection.

text: `Columns` defines each column width and optional header widget.
evidence: TableColumn has Width and Header fields, consumed by Build.

text: `RenderHeader` supplies each header, with the column's `Header` as the fallback when the callback returns nil.
evidence: Table.Build falls back to col.Header when RenderHeader returns nil.

text: The default renderer reads cells from slice or array rows.
evidence: Reflection handles Slice and Array values and formats the indexed element.

text: `RenderCell` receives the row, source row index, column index, and active and selected flags. A custom renderer controls the cell's appearance, including selection highlighting.
evidence: Calls the renderer with sourceRow and column, plus active/selected flags, and returns the supplied widget without adding cursor/selection styles.

text: `Filter` and `MatchCell` keep rows with a matching cell.
evidence: Each row is included if any column produces a matched result.

text: `RenderCellWithMatch` receives the matching data for each cell and takes precedence over `RenderCell`.
evidence: Build adapts RenderCell only when RenderCellWithMatch is nil; forwards per-cell cached match data.

text: `CursorIndex` and row indices passed to renderers and matchers refer to `State.Rows`, even after filtering or sorting.
evidence: Build maps each filtered/sorted view row back to its source row index; matchers receive original rows and indices before sorting.

text: `SetRows`, `Append`, `Prepend`, `InsertAt`, `RemoveAt`, `RemoveWhere`, and `Clear` update the data in `TableState`.
evidence: These exported state methods update Rows and reconcile applicable cursor/selection state.

text: Up and Down, or `k` and `j`, move between visible rows. Home and End move to the first and last visible rows.
evidence: Arrow and j/k handlers use viewIndices; home/end choose first/last visible row.

text: `TableSelectionCursor` highlights a cell by default. `TableSelectionRow` highlights a row, and `TableSelectionColumn` highlights a column.
evidence: Cursor is the zero enum value; active cells compare both coordinates, row only, or column only by mode.

text: Left and Right move between columns in cursor and column modes.
evidence: Horizontal keybinds are conditional on TableSelectionCursor or TableSelectionColumn.

text: With `MultiSelect`, Shift navigation and pointer selection extend the selection according to the selection mode.
evidence: Mode-specific Shift callbacks and extendSelectionTo select rows, columns, or a cell box.

text: Enter and a double-click call `OnSelect(row T)`, or `ActivateOnClick` enables single-click activation.
evidence: OnSelect accepts T; Enter, repeated clicks, and ActivateOnClick invoke it for the normalized cursor row.

text: Selection keys depend on the mode: row indices, column indices, or `rowIndex * len(Columns) + colIndex` for cells.
evidence: Row mode keys are row indices, column mode keys are column indices, cursor mode keys are row*columnCount+column.

text: `SelectedRow()` returns the cursor row and a boolean indicating whether it exists. `SelectedRows()` is intended for row-selection mode.
evidence: SelectedRow validates cursor bounds and returns T,bool; SelectedRows scans row indices and assumes row-based selection.

text: `NewTableState` tracks rows by position. `NewTableStateWithRowID(rows, rowID)` preserves the cursor and row or cell selections across `SetRows` when the same unique IDs remain.
evidence: Constructor installs an ID extractor; SetRows maps cursor and row/cell selection keys between old/new unique IDs.

text: The ID function must return stable, nonempty, unique strings without side effects. Empty, duplicate, or removed IDs lose their selections, and a cursor that cannot be preserved is clamped.
evidence: Constructor contract requires pure stable IDs; empty/duplicate IDs are not mapped, missing selections are dropped, and unmapped cursors are clamped.

text: `SetRows` performs identity reconciliation. Calling `State.Rows.Set(...)` directly bypasses it.
evidence: SetRows calls replaceIdentifiedRows when rowID is set; raw signal writes do not invoke the state method.

text: This example uses names as unique row IDs and enables sorting, resizing, and a frozen header.
evidence: The example extracts row[0] as ID, supplies a name comparator, marks that column resizable, and enables FrozenHeader.

text: Each sortable or resizable column needs a unique, nonempty `TableColumn.ID`.
evidence: Sorting and resizing reject empty IDs and IDs shared by more than one column.

text: `Comparators` maps column IDs to functions that return a negative value, zero, or a positive value for two rows.
evidence: Looks up comparator by ColumnID and tests its return value against zero for ordering.

text: Clicking a sortable header or pressing Ctrl+S cycles the current column through ascending, descending, and unsorted order.
evidence: Header clicks set CursorColumn and cycle ascending, descending, then zero/none. Table.Keybinds binds ctrl+s to cycleSort for CursorColumn.

text: `State.Sort.Set(TableSort{ColumnID: "name", Direction: TableSortAscending})` sets the sort programmatically.
evidence: Sort is Signal[TableSort]; Build reads its current value and passes it to sortedRows.

text: Sorting changes the visible order without changing `State.Rows`. Filtering runs first, and equal comparator results retain source order.
evidence: Build calls filteredRows first; sortedRows creates a separate permutation and uses source indices to break equal comparator results.

text: `TableSortNone` restores the filtered order, including fuzzy-match ranking when enabled.
evidence: Any direction other than ascending/descending returns the already-filtered rows and indices unchanged, retaining their fuzzy ranking.

text: `Resizable` enables dragging the rightmost cell of a column header and Ctrl+Left or Ctrl+Right on the current column. Ctrl+R restores its configured width.
evidence: Ctrl+left/right call resizeCurrent, ctrl+r calls resetCurrentWidth; table_features.go headerMouseDown starts a drag on the rightmost header cell.

text: `MinWidth` and `MaxWidth` constrain resized widths in cells. The minimum is at least one cell, and a zero maximum means unlimited.
evidence: Clamps to max(1,MinWidth); only applies MaxWidth when positive, with the minimum taking priority.

text: `State.ColumnWidths` stores width overrides by column ID.
evidence: Writes the clamped integer width to State.ColumnWidths under the column ID.

text: A shared `ScrollState` connects a regular table to a surrounding `Scrollable` for cursor visibility.
evidence: Without an owned viewport, revealCursor uses the supplied shared ScrollState for cursor visibility.

text: `FrozenHeader` keeps headers visible, and `FrozenColumns` keeps the first N columns visible during horizontal scrolling.
evidence: Viewport layout applies FrozenRows/FrozenColumns through clipViewportCells; Table.BuildContainerLayoutNode sets these from the frozen options.

text: Either frozen option gives the table its own viewport. A bounded `Style.Width` and `Style.Height` define its visible area without a surrounding `Scrollable`.
evidence: State plus FrozenHeader or positive FrozenColumns enables an owned viewport; table layout applies Style dimensions to its container.

text: The built-in viewport uses the supplied `ScrollState`, or an internal one when none is supplied. Alt+Left and Alt+Right pan horizontally by three cells.
evidence: Returns ScrollState when supplied, otherwise State.viewport; Table.Keybinds pans this state three cells for alt+left/right.

text: [List](list.md) displays one item per row without column definitions.
evidence: List builds a Column of item widgets and has no Columns field.

text: `Tree` displays hierarchical nodes with navigation and expansion.
evidence: Build flattens visible hierarchy and renders rows with expansion indicators.

text: An expanded Project node containing main.go and README.md, followed by Archive.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `NewTreeState` stores root nodes, the cursor path, collapsed nodes, and selection.
evidence: Constructor initializes Nodes, CursorPath, Collapsed, and Selection.

text: Each `TreeNode` holds `Data` and optional `Children`.
evidence: The struct contains Data T and Children []TreeNode[T].

text: Loaded nodes with children start expanded unless their state marks them collapsed.
evidence: Returns true for loaded expandable nodes unless State.IsCollapsed is true.

text: Up and Down move between visible nodes.
evidence: Bindings invoke keyCursorUp and keyCursorDown on view paths.

text: Left collapses a node or moves to its parent, while Right expands a node or moves to its first child.
evidence: This method and expandOrMoveToChild implement the conditional actions.

text: Space toggles expansion.
evidence: Both space spellings bind toggleExpansion.

text: Enter and a double-click on a node's label invoke `OnSelect(node T, selected []T)` with the cursor node and the selected nodes.
evidence: selectNode passes cursor data and getSelectedNodes to the two-argument OnSelect callback; label double-click invokes it.

text: `ActivateOnClick` enables single-click activation on a node label. A click on its expansion indicator toggles expansion instead.
evidence: Checks indicator hit regions before activation; label activation uses ActivateOnClick or a repeated click.

text: `MultiSelect` enables range selection with Shift navigation, Shift-click, and dragging.
evidence: Conditional keybindings extend selection; mouse handlers use MultiSelect for range selection.

text: `NodeID` supplies stable identifiers for collapsed and selected nodes. Without it, identifiers are based on node paths.
evidence: Uses nonempty NodeID results, otherwise pathKey(path); collapse and selection use these IDs.

text: `CursorPath` and `TreeNodeContext.Path` contain source child indices, starting at the root, even when a filter hides other nodes.
evidence: filterVisible builds paths by appending source child indices, not positions in the filtered output.

text: `ClearSelection` clears selected nodes. `ClearAnchor` resets the starting point for the next Shift selection without clearing the current selection.
evidence: ClearSelection resets Selection, ClearAnchor only resets anchorPath, and the next shift move sets a missing anchor to the cursor.

text: `RenderNode` receives the data and a `TreeNodeContext` containing depth, path, expansion, and selection information.
evidence: Struct fields provide these values and RenderNode accepts this type.

text: `Filter` keeps matching loaded nodes and their ancestors, including matches under collapsed parents. It does not load children to search them.
evidence: Recurses over existing Children without checking collapsed state or invoking OnExpand; includes matching nodes and ancestors.

text: `RenderNodeWithMatch` also receives the match result.
evidence: Field signature includes MatchResult.

text: For lazy loading, a nil `Children` slice uses `HasChildren` to determine whether the node can expand.
evidence: When Children is nil, nodeExpandable delegates to HasChildren.

text: `OnExpand` receives a callback that installs the loaded children.
evidence: Passes a callback that calls State.SetChildren for the node path.

text: `ShowGuideLines`, `Indent`, and the indicator fields control the hierarchy markers. Guide lines are enabled by default, and the default indent is two cells.
evidence: Nonpositive Indent defaults to 2; nil ShowGuideLines defaults to true; indicator fields control expanded/collapsed/leaf labels.

text: A shared `ScrollState` connects the tree to a surrounding `Scrollable` for cursor visibility.
evidence: Computes cursor row region and reveals it using ScrollState.

text: [DirectoryTree](directorytree.md) adds filesystem defaults to `Tree`.
evidence: Supplies path IDs, name matching, directory expansion, and loading.

text: `DirectoryTree` displays filesystem entries through `Tree[DirectoryEntry]`.
evidence: Embeds Tree[DirectoryEntry] and Build delegates to its resolved Tree.

text: A DirectoryTree with an expanded project directory and two sample files.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: The first snippet browses the current directory, while the image and registered demo use the preloaded sample below.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `NewDirectoryTreeState` creates a single root, while `NewDirectoryTreeStateWithRoots` accepts multiple paths.
evidence: Loops over supplied root paths and passes the resulting nodes to NewTreeState.

text: The embedded `Tree` holds state, callbacks, filtering, selection, and scroll configuration.
evidence: Embeds Tree[DirectoryEntry], whose fields carry those settings.

text: Expanding an unloaded directory reads its children in a goroutine.
evidence: resolvedTree installs OnExpand; loadChildren launches a goroutine that calls readChildren.

text: The default `ReadDir` uses `os.ReadDir`, while a custom function can provide entries from another source.
evidence: Selects d.ReadDir or defaultDirectoryReadDir, which invokes os.ReadDir.

text: Entries whose names start with a dot are excluded unless `IncludeHidden` is true.
evidence: Skips dot-prefixed names when IncludeHidden is false.

text: The default order puts directories first, then sorts names without case sensitivity.
evidence: Compares IsDir first, then directoryEntrySortKey, which lowercases Name.

text: `Sort` replaces the default ordering.
evidence: Calls d.Sort when non-nil, otherwise defaultDirectorySort.

text: `EagerLoad` recursively loads unloaded descendants in the background and collapses newly loaded directories that have children.
evidence: eagerLoad calls Collapse only when len(children)>0.

text: A read error appears as an error node.
evidence: Returns a directoryTreeErrorNode when ReadDir returns an error.

text: The default labels use `D` for directories, `F` for files, and `!` for errors.
evidence: Selects these exact icon strings before the label.

text: Filtering matches entry names, and node identifiers default to entry paths.
evidence: Default MatchNode uses entry.Name and NodeID returns entry.Path.

text: Filtering searches only loaded nodes. `EagerLoad` makes descendants available to filtering as their directory reads complete.
evidence: Eager loading recursively installs Children with SetChildren, making them visible to Tree filtering; matching itself only walks loaded nodes.

text: [Tree](tree.md) describes the shared navigation and selection behavior.
evidence: Keybinds and mouse methods delegate to the resolved Tree.

text: `TabBar` displays horizontal tabs, and `TabView` adds the active tab's content below the bar.
evidence: Constructs a Column with TabBar and Switcher keyed by ActiveKey.

text: Home and Settings tabs with the Home content visible.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `TabState` stores the tabs and the active key.
evidence: Contains tabs and activeKey signals.

text: `NewTabState` activates the first tab when the list is nonempty.
evidence: Initial activeKey is tabs[0].Key when len(tabs)>0.

text: Each `Tab` has a unique `Key`, a visible `Label`, and optional `Content`.
evidence: Field declarations describe key identity, label, and content.

text: `TabBar` ignores `Content`, while `TabView` uses it for the selected view.
evidence: TabBar builds labels while TabView maps Content widgets by Key.

text: Left and Right, or `h` and `l`, select adjacent tabs and wrap at the ends.
evidence: Bindings call selectPrevious/selectNext, whose state methods wrap indices.

text: `KeybindPattern` supports plain, Alt, or Ctrl number keys for the first nine tabs. The default, `TabKeybindNone`, disables number shortcuts.
evidence: Zero-valued TabKeybindNone disables position bindings; other patterns create bindings for at most nine tabs.

text: Clicking a tab activates it.
evidence: Tab label Click callback sets active key and invokes OnTabChange.

text: `Closable` adds close buttons and Ctrl+W.
evidence: Adds ctrl+w when Closable; tabItem.Build adds close control.

text: If `OnTabClose` is set, it handles closure instead of the bar calling `RemoveTab`.
evidence: Invokes callback if present, otherwise State.RemoveTab; button closure matches this behavior.

text: `AllowReorder` enables Ctrl+H and Ctrl+L to move the active tab.
evidence: Adds ctrl+h and ctrl+l mapped to moveActiveLeft/right.

text: `AddTab`, `InsertTab`, `RemoveTab`, and `SetLabel` update tabs through `TabState`.
evidence: These methods update the tabs signal.

text: `TabStyle` and `ActiveTabStyle` customize the inactive and active tabs.
evidence: Selects TabStyle or ActiveTabStyle according to active state before constructing tabItem.

text: `TabView.ContentStyle` styles the content area.
evidence: Copies ContentStyle into the Switcher style.

text: [Switcher](switcher.md) displays content selected by a string key.
evidence: Active key selects a child from the Children map.

text: `Breadcrumbs` displays a path as text segments separated by a configurable separator.
evidence: Loops over Path and inserts separator Text widgets between labels.

text: Projects, Terma, and Docs breadcrumbs above a selection message.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `Path` supplies the segment labels in display order.
evidence: Ranges over Path from index zero and appends each label.

text: `Separator` defaults to `>` with one space on either side.
evidence: Empty separator becomes > and is wrapped with spaces.

text: `OnSelect` makes each segment clickable and receives its zero-based index, including the final segment.
evidence: Installs a Text.Click callback for every segment if OnSelect is non-nil.

text: The callback determines what navigation occurs.
evidence: The click handler only calls b.OnSelect(index); it does not mutate Path or route elsewhere.

text: Without `OnSelect`, the segments are plain text.
evidence: Appends Text without a Click callback when OnSelect is nil.

text: An empty path renders an `EmptyWidget`.
evidence: Returns EmptyWidget when len(Path)==0.

text: The default colors distinguish clickable ancestors, the final segment, and separators.
evidence: Uses theme.Link for earlier clickable segments, theme.Text otherwise, and theme.TextMuted for separators.

text: `Style.ForegroundColor` overrides these default colors.
evidence: Theme colors are chosen only when the copied style foreground is unset.

text: When `ID` is set, clickable segments receive IDs formed as `<ID>-segment-<index>`.
evidence: Uses fmt.Sprintf with %s-segment-%d when OnSelect is non-nil and ID is nonempty.

text: A table with a sortable Name header and Mina, Leon, and Ada rows.
evidence: The registered TableControls example supplies the three named rows and a comparator for the Name header; the generated SVG shows the unsorted indicator.

text: Run this example with `go run ./docs/widget-examples -widget table-controls`.
evidence: The -widget flag selects an entry by Name and runs its Widget; collections.Examples registers TableControls under table-controls.

text: `KeybindBar` displays keybindings from the focused widget and its ancestors.
evidence: Calls ctx.ActiveKeybinds, which collects the focused chain through FocusManager.

text: A Save button, its status, and a keybinding bar.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: The bar updates when focus changes or reactive state read by `Keybinds` changes.
evidence: Test changes input selection and verifies Copy appears and disappears in the bar.

text: Bindings with `Hidden` set are omitted.
evidence: Skips kb.Hidden before building visible groups.

text: Among visible bindings, duplicate keys appear once, with the focused widget taking precedence over ancestors.
evidence: Build skips Hidden before marking a key as seen; ActiveKeybinds orders focused bindings before ancestor bindings.

text: Consecutive bindings with the same `Name` share one label, with their keys joined by `/`.
evidence: Groups adjacent matching names and joins their keys using strings.Join with slash.

text: Hints that do not fit are omitted from the end rather than truncated.
evidence: Stops before the first whole hint that would exceed ctx.Width.

text: The default width is `Flex(1)`, and the default height is one cell.
evidence: Unset dimensions resolve to Flex(1) and Cells(1).

text: `FormatKey` changes the displayed key names.
evidence: Invokes custom FormatKey when set.

text: Without a formatter, a literal space becomes `space`, and other keys keep their names.
evidence: Only maps the literal space key; returns other strings unchanged.

text: `Style` controls the bar's appearance.
evidence: Passes Style into the rendered Text.

text: [Jumper](jumper.md) exposes its jump toggle in the keybinding bar.
evidence: Returns a non-hidden Jump binding for the toggle key.

text: `Jumper` adds labeled keyboard targets to its child widget.
evidence: Registers jumpOverlay while active and returns Child.

text: Jump mode labels a folder list and its visible items.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: The image and registered demo start with jump mode active through the preview function below.
evidence: The compiled example constructs the stated widgets and sample content.

text: `NewJumpState` creates inactive jump state.
evidence: Initializes active to false and typed to an empty string.

text: Ctrl+O toggles jump mode by default, and `Key` changes this binding.
evidence: Returns DefaultJumpKey ctrl+o when Key is empty.

text: `Targets` assigns fixed keys to widget IDs.
evidence: Key and ID define each static target; overlay resolves targets by ID.

text: A static target on a focusable widget moves focus to it, while a container target focuses its first focusable descendant.
evidence: Static resolution uses a focusable target or the first candidate contained in its bounds.

text: A target with an `Action` calls it instead of changing focus.
evidence: Action branch calls action and returns before RequestFocus.

text: Static keys can contain multiple characters, but one key must not prefix another.
evidence: Exact matches execute immediately before prefix matching, making longer prefixed keys unreachable.

text: `Dynamic` adds hints to visible list items, tree nodes, table rows or cells, tabs, and other jump targets.
evidence: Dynamic collection uses Jumpable items and remaining focusable widgets; builtin widgets implement Jump.

text: A static target on a non-focusable `Jumpable` item invokes its jump behavior.
evidence: resolveJumpLabels checks direct focusable candidates first, then resolves a non-focusable Jumpable through jumpItem, whose action calls Jump.

text: Custom widgets implement `Jumpable` with a `Jump()` method.
evidence: The interface contains Jump().

text: `Hints` supplies the characters for dynamic labels.
evidence: Dynamic label generation selects Hints or DefaultJumpHints.

text: Typing part of a label narrows the hints, and Backspace removes the last typed character.
evidence: Prefix match updates typed and backspace removes the last rune.

text: Escape, the toggle key, a click, or an unmatched key leaves jump mode.
evidence: Escape/toggle/unmatched input deactivate; jump overlay mouse handler deactivates on click.

text: Only visible targets receive labels. When focus is inside a trap, jumps stay within that trap.
evidence: resolveJumpLabels derives trapID from the currently focused entry, then restricts candidates and item holders to that scope.

text: `State.Activate()` enters jump mode programmatically.
evidence: Clears typed and sets active true.

text: `State.IsActive()` and `State.Typed()` read reactive state.
evidence: IsActive and Typed use signal Get.

text: `LabelStyle` changes label styling, and `Backdrop` controls the tint behind labels.
evidence: Fields are consumed by overlay rendering for label style and backdrop color.

text: [Tabs](tabs.md) provides `TabBar.TabID` for targeting an individual tab.
evidence: Returns a stable ID derived from the bar ID and tab key.

text: Create state once with `NewJumpState` and reuse it across builds.
evidence: The constructor allocates fresh signals and initial state; calling it in each Build would discard the current state.
